title: Deep-learning-guided mining of NRPS scaffolds yields active naturally inspired antimicrobial peptides
summary: The team mined 216,408 bacterial genomes, identifying 335,024 NRPS clusters and 328 dereplicated peptide scaffolds. Deep-learning scoring selected five synthesized peptides; P2 showed MIC50 values of 1–2 μM against Vibrio parahaemolyticus and V. alginolyticus. Deep-learning-guided sequence optimization produced P2.2, which showed increased antibacterial activity, membrane effects and reduced hemolysis in assays.
ai_technology: Deep-learning peptide activity scoring and sequence-optimization algorithms
organization: Zhejiang University of Technology and collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: Deep-learning-guided sequence optimization produced P2.2, which showed increased antibacterial activity, membrane effects and reduced hemolysis in assays.
evidence.unknown: The study calls the peptides naturally inspired; it did not establish that the synthesized sequences are the native products of the mined clusters. P2's MIC50 of 1–2 μM did not mean 80% inhibition: its MIC80 exceeded 128 μM under the reported 24-hour conditions. P2.2's measured MIC80 values were 32 μM for V. parahaemolyticus and 64 μM for V. alginolyticus. These are in-vitro findings, not clinical efficacy.
evidence.ai_role: AI-ranked peptide candidates inspired by nonribosomal peptide synthetase cluster scaffolds from bacterial genomes and guided amino-acid optimization of P2 into P2.2; the selected sequences were synthesized and tested in vitro.
